\chapter{Water and a View}
\label{ch:ml-water-and-a-view}
\hlchaptermodality{484}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say drinking water, to boil and cool, to purify, a window and a view.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 484: I can say drinking water, to boil and cool, to purify, a window and a view.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കുടിവെള്ളം} (kuṭiveḷḷaṁ)}{കുടിവെള്ളം (kuṭiveḷḷaṁ)}]{\ml{കുടിവെള്ളം} (kuṭiveḷḷaṁ) — drinking water}

\label{lesson:ML-C484-kutivellam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a menu, then the Malayalam for a waiter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കുടിവെള്ളം}}
\textbf{\ml{കുടിവെള്ളം}} — \emph{kuṭiveḷḷaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}drinking water\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{യാത്രയിൽ} \ml{ഞങ്ങൾ} \ml{കുടിവെള്ളം} \ml{കൊണ്ടുപോയി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yātrayil ñaṅṅaḷ kuṭiveḷḷaṁ koṇṭupōyi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We took drinking water on the journey.
\end{quote}

\ml{കുടി}-, drinking, from \ml{കുടിക്കുക}, plus \ml{വെള്ളം}, water.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കുടിവെള്ളം}} (\emph{kuṭiveḷḷaṁ}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{കുടി}, drinking, from \ml{കുടിക്കുക} (DEDR 1654), and \ml{വെള്ളം}, water.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṭiveḷḷaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṭiveḷḷaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yātrayil ñaṅṅaḷ kuṭiveḷḷaṁ koṇṭupōyi.} — We took drinking water on the journey.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a menu, then the Malayalam for a waiter, then say \emph{kuṭiveḷḷaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കുടിവെള്ളം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Drinking water\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റുക} (tiḷappiccāṟṟuka)}{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റുക (tiḷappiccāṟṟuka)}]{\ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റുക} (tiḷappiccāṟṟuka) — to boil and cool}

\label{lesson:ML-C484-tilappiccarruka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a waiter, then the Malayalam for drinking water.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റുക}}
\textbf{\ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റുക}} — \emph{tiḷappiccāṟṟuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to boil and cool\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അമ്മ} \ml{കുടിവെള്ളം} \ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{amma kuṭiveḷḷaṁ tiḷappiccāṟṟi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mother boiled the drinking water and let it cool.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റി}, \emph{tiḷappiccāṟṟi}.

One verb for a habit of the house: \ml{തിളപ്പിച്ച്}, having boiled, plus \ml{ആറ്റുക}, to cool.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റുക}} (\emph{tiḷappiccāṟṟuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{തിളപ്പിക്കുക}, to boil (DEDR 3257), and \ml{ആറ്റുക}, to cool (DEDR 404).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiḷappiccāṟṟuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiḷappiccāṟṟuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amma kuṭiveḷḷaṁ tiḷappiccāṟṟi.} — Mother boiled the drinking water and let it cool.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a waiter, then the Malayalam for drinking water, then say \emph{tiḷappiccāṟṟuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To boil and cool\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുക} (śuddhīkarikkuka)}{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുക (śuddhīkarikkuka)}]{\ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുക} (śuddhīkarikkuka) — to purify}

\label{lesson:ML-C484-suddhikarikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for drinking water, then the Malayalam for to boil and cool.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുക}} — \emph{śuddhīkarikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to purify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആ} \ml{യന്ത്രം} \ml{കിണറ്റിലെ} \ml{വെള്ളം} \ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā yantraṁ kiṇaṟṟile veḷḷaṁ śuddhīkarikkunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That machine purifies the well water.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിച്ചു}, \emph{śuddhīkariccu}.

\ml{ശുദ്ധം}, pure, plus -\ml{ീകരിക്കുക}, to make: the same ending makes many formal verbs.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുക}} (\emph{śuddhīkarikkuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{śuddha}, \textquotedblleft{}clean, pure\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with \emph{-īkaraṇa}, making into, and the Malayalam verb ending.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śuddhīkarikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śuddhīkarikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā yantraṁ kiṇaṟṟile veḷḷaṁ śuddhīkarikkunnu.} — That machine purifies the well water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for drinking water, then the Malayalam for to boil and cool, then say \emph{śuddhīkarikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To purify\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ജനൽ} (janal)}{ജനൽ (janal)}]{\ml{ജനൽ} (janal) — a window}

\label{lesson:ML-C484-janal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to boil and cool, then the Malayalam for to purify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ജനൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{ജനൽ}} — \emph{janal} — \textquotedblleft{}a window\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{തീവണ്ടിയുടെ} \ml{ജനലിലൂടെ} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{വയലുകൾ} \ml{കണ്ടു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tīvaṇṭiyuṭe janalilūṭe ñān vayalukaḷ kaṇṭu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Through the train window I saw the paddy fields.
\end{quote}

Also spelt \ml{ജനാല}. A window seat is a \ml{ജനലിനടുത്തുള്ള} \ml{സീറ്റ്}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ജനൽ}} (\emph{janal}) was borrowed from Portuguese \emph{janela}, a window, one of the words the Portuguese left on the Malabar coast.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{janal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{janal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīvaṇṭiyuṭe janalilūṭe ñān vayalukaḷ kaṇṭu.} — Through the train window I saw the paddy fields.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to boil and cool, then the Malayalam for to purify, then say \emph{janal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ജനൽ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A window\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കാഴ്ച} (kāḻca)}{കാഴ്ച (kāḻca)}]{\ml{കാഴ്ച} (kāḻca) — a view; a sight}

\label{lesson:ML-C484-kalca}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to purify, then the Malayalam for a window.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കാഴ്ച}}
\textbf{\ml{കാഴ്ച}} — \emph{kāḻca} — \textquotedblleft{}a view; a sight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മലമുകളിൽ} \ml{നിന്നുള്ള} \ml{കാഴ്ച} \ml{വളരെ} \ml{സുന്ദരമായിരുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{malamukaḷil ninnuḷḷa kāḻca vaḷare sundaramāyirunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The view from the hilltop was very beautiful.
\end{quote}

The noun of \ml{കാണുക}, to see. It also means eyesight.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കാഴ്ച}} (\emph{kāḻca}) is native Dravidian, the noun of \ml{കാണുക}, to see; DEDR lists it as eyesight and a spectacle (DEDR 1443).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāḻca}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāḻca}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malamukaḷil ninnuḷḷa kāḻca vaḷare sundaramāyirunnu.} — The view from the hilltop was very beautiful.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to purify, then the Malayalam for a window, then say \emph{kāḻca} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കാഴ്ച} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A view; a sight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 477–484 — a review}

\label{lesson:ML-R484-review-477-484}



\begin{quote}
Say the Malayalam for a landing place and a riverbank.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a landing place, a riverbank, a canal, to swim across, to dash forward
  \item a tourist, a guide, a destination, an itinerary, to roam around
  \item to wander, to stay over, a fellow traveller, a stopover, to pass by
  \item a travelogue, to leave behind, to ask around, a locker, to keep aside
  \item a resort, an inn, accommodation, a resident, a reception desk
  \item to hire, a security deposit, to vacate, to refund, an arrangement
  \item a service, a mosquito net, hygiene, a menu, a waiter
  \item drinking water, to boil and cool, to purify, a window, a view
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A landing place? (\textbf{\ml{കടവ്}}, \emph{kaṭavŭ}.) A riverbank? (\textbf{\ml{പുഴയോരം}}, \emph{puḻayōraṁ}.) A canal? (\textbf{\ml{കനാൽ}}, \emph{kanāl}.) To swim across? (\textbf{\ml{നീന്തിക്കടക്കുക}}, \emph{nīntikkaṭakkuka}.) To dash forward? (\textbf{\ml{കുതിക്കുക}}, \emph{kutikkuka}.) A tourist? (\textbf{\ml{വിനോദസഞ്ചാരി}}, \emph{vinōdasañcāri}.) A guide? (\textbf{\ml{വഴികാട്ടി}}, \emph{vaḻikāṭṭi}.) A destination? (\textbf{\ml{ലക്ഷ്യസ്ഥാനം}}, \emph{lakṣyasthānaṁ}.) An itinerary? (\textbf{\ml{യാത്രാപരിപാടി}}, \emph{yātrāparipāṭi}.) To roam around? (\textbf{\ml{ചുറ്റിക്കറങ്ങുക}}, \emph{cuṟṟikkaṟaṅṅuka}.) To wander? (\textbf{\ml{അലയുക}}, \emph{alayuka}.) To stay over? (\textbf{\ml{തങ്ങുക}}, \emph{taṅṅuka}.) A fellow traveller? (\textbf{\ml{സഹയാത്രികൻ}}, \emph{sahayātrikan}.) A stopover? (\textbf{\ml{ഇടത്താവളം}}, \emph{iṭattāvaḷaṁ}.) To pass by? (\textbf{\ml{പിന്നിടുക}}, \emph{pinniṭuka}.) A travelogue? (\textbf{\ml{യാത്രാവിവരണം}}, \emph{yātrāvivaraṇaṁ}.) To leave behind? (\textbf{\ml{മറന്നുവയ്ക്കുക}}, \emph{maṟannuvaykkuka}.) To ask around? (\textbf{\ml{ചോദിച്ചറിയുക}}, \emph{cōdiccaṟiyuka}.) A locker? (\textbf{\ml{ലോക്കർ}}, \emph{lōkkar}.) To keep aside? (\textbf{\ml{കരുതിവയ്ക്കുക}}, \emph{karutivaykkuka}.) A resort? (\textbf{\ml{റിസോർട്ട്}}, \emph{ṟisōrṭṭŭ}.) An inn? (\textbf{\ml{സത്രം}}, \emph{satraṁ}.) Accommodation? (\textbf{\ml{താമസസ്ഥലം}}, \emph{tāmasasthalaṁ}.) A resident? (\textbf{\ml{താമസക്കാരൻ}}, \emph{tāmasakkāran}.) A reception desk? (\textbf{\ml{റിസപ്ഷൻ}}, \emph{ṟisapṣan}.) To hire? (\textbf{\ml{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുക്കുക}}, \emph{vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka}.) A security deposit? (\textbf{\ml{നിക്ഷേപം}}, \emph{nikṣēpaṁ}.) To vacate? (\textbf{\ml{ഒഴിയുക}}, \emph{oḻiyuka}.) To refund? (\textbf{\ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകുക}}, \emph{tiriccunalkuka}.) An arrangement? (\textbf{\ml{ഏർപ്പാട്}}, \emph{ērppāṭŭ}.) A service? (\textbf{\ml{സേവനം}}, \emph{sēvanaṁ}.) A mosquito net? (\textbf{\ml{കൊതുകുവല}}, \emph{kotukuvala}.) Hygiene? (\textbf{\ml{ശുചിത്വം}}, \emph{śucitvaṁ}.) A menu? (\textbf{\ml{മെനു}}, \emph{menu}.) A waiter? (\textbf{\ml{വെയിറ്റർ}}, \emph{veyiṟṟar}.) Drinking water? (\textbf{\ml{കുടിവെള്ളം}}, \emph{kuṭiveḷḷaṁ}.) To boil and cool? (\textbf{\ml{തിളപ്പിച്ചാറ്റുക}}, \emph{tiḷappiccāṟṟuka}.) To purify? (\textbf{\ml{ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കുക}}, \emph{śuddhīkarikkuka}.) A window? (\textbf{\ml{ജനൽ}}, \emph{janal}.) A view? (\textbf{\ml{കാഴ്ച}}, \emph{kāḻca}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
